sources.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400 – Mathematical methods for the physical sciences, Spring 2023
sources.locator: Complete 7-page PDF, inspected pp. 1–7: equation (1), Gaussian localization in Examples 1, 3, and 4, the endpoint example in Example 2, and the nonquadratic phase in Example 3.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete seven-page PDF in the full-text reader. It gives the large-parameter setup and worked Gaussian and boundary/nonquadratic examples. Its replacements of the integrand by a local approximation are heuristic; the submitted Laplace theorem and examples supply complete local arguments under their stated hypotheses. The plan describes an eight-page UConn note; this retrieved matching-titled UConn note has seven PDF pages, and that page-count discrepancy is recorded for reconciliation.

contents.name: Large-parameter Laplace integral and local Gaussian approximation
contents.support: The note motivates localization and the Gaussian scaling. The local proof adds measurability, quadratic domination, dominated convergence, and the off-mode bound rather than importing the heuristic step.

contents.name: Exact one-dimensional Gaussian phase calculation
contents.support: The example independently evaluates the Gaussian integral exactly by the published Gaussian-integral supplier and a justified affine substitution.

contents.name: Boundary-dominated mode example
contents.support: The source exhibits a boundary contribution with a different scale; the finite witness and its rate comparison are proved locally.

contents.name: Nonquadratic phase and changed concentration power
contents.support: The note shows that nonquadratic local phase order changes the scale. The interior singular-mode witness is an independent direct lower bound.

contents.name: Steepest contribution near a single dominant mode
contents.locator: pp. 1–7, complete note, including the single-maximum setup preceding equation (2)
contents.support: The note's single-dominant-mode framing motivates the warning; the two-half-interval calculation is proved locally from the authored theorem.

sources.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
sources.locator: Complete §2.3(iii), equations (2.3.13)–(2.3.18), including conditions (a)–(c) and the notes on source error references.
sources.reading_verification: Read the full §2.3(iii) text and its listed conditions. This DLMF treatment is a one-dimensional endpoint-minimum expansion and points to Olver/Boyd for error proofs; it is used only for its stated regime and warnings. The multidimensional compact-domain statement is proved locally.

contents.name: Laplace integral, endpoint localization, and asymptotic expansion
contents.support: This supplies an independent asymptotic treatment in a distinct one-dimensional endpoint convention; no DLMF formula or proof is imported into the local multidimensional theorem.

contents.name: Endpoint mode is a separate asymptotic regime
contents.support: The stated endpoint theorem underscores why an interior Gaussian formula cannot be transferred without checking the boundary regime; the counterexample is calculated locally.

contents.name: Local phase and amplitude orders affect the scale
contents.support: The local power parameters in the DLMF expansion show that quadratic nondegeneracy determines the Gaussian scale; the witness itself is proved locally.

contents.name: Localization at dominant modes
contents.support: The source isolates one dominant endpoint; the example proves directly that two equal modes contribute two leading terms.

sources.title: Francis Bach, Approximating Integrals with Laplace's Method
sources.locator: Complete online note; opening compact-domain assumptions and the multidimensional Hessian/Jacobian derivation.
sources.reading_verification: Read the full note and inspected its compact-domain setup, unique strict minimizer, positive-definite Hessian, Taylor approximation, and matrix square-root Jacobian. It is an explanatory derivation; the local proof supplies the exact integrable majorant, measurable-amplitude treatment, and global off-mode estimate.

contents.name: Compact multidimensional Laplace expression and Hessian determinant factor
contents.locator: Opening assumptions and displayed change of variables $y=√t H^{1/2}(x-x_*)$
contents.support: Supports the determinant scaling in the Gaussian factor; the local lemma supplies a full Cholesky/change-of-variables proof under Countable Choice.

contents.name: Unique strict mode and local quadratic approximation
contents.locator: Opening compact-domain assumptions and displayed approximation of $I(t)$
contents.support: An independent multidimensional treatment aligns with the mode/Hessian convention; the complete proof adds the dominated-convergence and tail steps.

contents.name: Single strict mode is part of the local formula's scope
contents.locator: Opening compact-domain assumptions, strict global minimizer bullet
contents.support: The example computes both equal-mode contributions and proves the factor two locally.

sources.title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, Julia edition
sources.locator: Complete online Chapter 5 §5.6 inspected, especially equations (5.6.1)–(5.6.4), Function 5.6.4, and Observation 5.6.6.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete online numerical-integration chapter and the full trapezoid section. It derives the equal-mesh weights by integrating the piecewise-linear interpolant and notes second-order accuracy. It does not supply the exact 1/12 derivative-bound proof used here; the local interpolation lemma and theorem provide it.

contents.support: The formula and endpoint half-weights match the authored definition; the definition states its domain explicitly.

contents.locator: Observation 5.6.6 and the error behavior following equation (5.6.4)
contents.support: Supports the second-order scale; the exact constant and proof are supplied locally from the interpolation error.

contents.name: A one-panel exactness-bound witness
contents.locator: Trapezoid formula and its local error discussion in §5.6
contents.support: The example computes the square-function witness directly and checks equality in the local bound.
